items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 14 at 5:04PM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
Patchy freezing fog is possible through much of the night for an
area stretching northwestward from Tok to Nenana, including the
Fairbanks Metro Area, which may cause a light slippery glaze to
form on surfaces. Use extra caution if you must travel through
the night.

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 14 at 5:04PM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
Moderate snow and winds are expected in the Eastern Brooks Range
through Saturday night. Total snow accumulations could range
between 2 and 5 inches during this time. Wind gusts to 35 mph
could produce areas of blowing and drifting snow. Travel may
become difficult throughout this period.

items.headline: High Wind Watch issued November 14 at 12:31PM AKST until November 17 at 6:00AM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
* WHAT...West winds 50 to 65 mph with gusts up to 80 mph possible.

* WHERE...Shemya and Attu Islands.

* WHEN...From Monday evening through late Monday night.

* IMPACTS...High winds could move loose debris, damage property, and
cause power outages. Travel could be difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Winds rapidly increase in strength late Monday
evening and peak Tuesday morning as a strong low pressure system
moves through the Bering. Winds will gradually lighten through
Tuesday afternoon.
items.instruction:
A high wind watch means there is potential for a hazardous high wind
event. Monitor the latest forecasts and warnings for updates on this
situation. Fasten loose objects or shelter objects in a safe location
prior to the onset of winds.
